Amorous

/AM-er-uhs/ - the stress falls on AM · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Amorous means showing romantic love or attraction.

The novel's two lighthouse keepers grow openly amorous by the final chapters, signaling their affection across the bay each night.

Worked Example

Every spring the park's swans put on an amorous display: necks curved toward each other, synchronized glides, and a fierce devotion that lasts the whole season. Photographers line the pond for it.

Amorous describes the showing of romantic love — glances, courtship, love letters. It is narrower and stronger than 'affectionate,' which covers any warm attachment: a grandmother's hug is affectionate, never amorous.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

romantic: can describe moods, settings, or people; broader and softer

smitten: suddenly and completely taken with someone — the falling itself

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

platonic: affectionate but purely friendly, with no romance in it

unromantic: without any romantic feeling or charm

Where it sits · how completely the attraction takes over — fond → amorous → besotted

fond vs. amorous: Fond is far milder than amorous — you can be fond of a cousin or a corner café, while amorous behavior announces romantic attraction.

besotted vs. amorous: Besotted goes further than amorous — an amorous suitor writes the letters, while a besotted one can no longer think about anything else.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — amor-

Root — amor-: love (Latin amor)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Amor- ('love') + -ous ('full of') = full of love. Latin amor is the romance root itself — the same family behind amiable and amicable — but amorous kept the narrowest share of it: not friendship, but romantic love on open display.

Use the root in a new word: enamored

Use the root in a new word: enamored: Visitors leave the glassblower's studio enamored of the craft — literally 'in love' with it, from en- (in) + amor (love).

Root Check

Word Choice

literary / slightly formal

Amorous is the observer's word for romance on display — amorous glances, an amorous subplot. In everyday speech 'romantic' or 'lovestruck' sounds more natural. Keep amorous for behavior, not settings: a couple is amorous; a candlelit café is romantic.
